the use of multivariate statistics and GIS-based approaches to interpret regional geochemical surveys can be very helpful in identifying the sources of heavy metal contamination in soils.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

a correct geochemical data treatment and the application of geostatistical methods to the data, together with the use of GIS software to compare data and maps with the regional database, are essential for a correct interpretation of regional data sets.

the knowledge of the regional background values is essential to assess human impact on the environment, but it is not enough to identify the anthropic vs natural origin of heavy metals and their sources.

the knowledge of regional background values and of the main factors controlling the regional variability of heavy metals in soils is a fundamental step to define realistic and useful guide values and to assess the environmental impact of human activities.
The main takeaway from our work is that

a multivariate and GIS-based approach, integrating statistical, geostatistical and geochemical methods, provides a powerful tool for the identification of heavy metals sources and the definition of regional background values.

the use of GIS and geostatistical methods is a very useful tool for the interpretation of the geochemical data, and for the definition of the background and the anthropogenic values of potentially harmful elements in soil.

the use of multivariate statistics and GIS-based geochemical mapping is a useful tool to identify and quantify the sources of heavy metals in soils, to evaluate the regional variability, and to identify the natural and anthropic sources of contamination.
